q: The physics describing motion, called ____, was discussed in the previous chapter.
e: Kinematics is the branch of physics that describes motion without considering the forces that cause it.

q: This chapter is dealt with ____ which explains motion in relation to the physical factors that affect motion such as force, momentum, mass etc.
e: Dynamics is the branch of mechanics concerned with the motion of bodies under the action of forces.

q: A fundamental concept in dynamics is ____.
e: Force is a push or pull that can change the state of motion of an object.

q: Force is defined precisely by ____.
e: Newton's three laws provide the exact mathematical and conceptual definition of force.

q: Force can change the ____ of an object.
e: A net force is required to change an object's state of rest or uniform motion.

q: Newton's first law states that: When no ____ acts upon it, a particle at rest will remain at rest and a particle in motion at a constant velocity will continue to move with the same constant velocity.
e: An object will maintain its state of motion unless acted upon by a net external force.

q: In mathematical form, If ____ then $a=0$, $v=$ constant (or) zero.
e: Zero net external force results in zero acceleration, meaning velocity remains constant.

q: Newton's first law expresses the idea of ____.
e: Inertia is the tendency of an object to resist changes in its state of motion.

q: ____ is the natural property of a body which resists the change of its state of motion.
e: Inertia is directly related to the mass of the body.

q: In fact, the first law is often referred as the ____.
e: Newton's first law is synonymous with the law of inertia because it describes this fundamental property.

q: The net external force acting upon a particle is equal to the ____ of particle.
c: product of the mass and the acceleration
e: This is the core statement of Newton's second law of motion.

q: In mathematical form, ____
e: This equation mathematically represents Newton's second law, relating force, mass, and acceleration.

q: The direction of the acceleration is the same as that of the ____.
e: Acceleration is a vector quantity that always points in the same direction as the net external force.

q: It is equivalent to say that acceleration is ____ to force.
e: As the magnitude of the net force increases, the acceleration of the particle increases accordingly.

q: Therefore, second law is also called ____.
e: The second law directly relates the net force applied to an object to its resulting acceleration.

q: Newton's third law of motion states that: Whenever two particles interact, the force exerted by the second on the first is ____ to the force exerted by the first on the second.
c: equal in magnitude and opposite in direction
e: Forces always occur in pairs that are equal in size but opposite in direction.

q: In other words, for every action, there is an ____.
e: This is the common phrasing of Newton's third law of motion.

q: Action-reaction pair does not act on a single object but acts on ____.
e: Because action and reaction forces act on different objects, they do not cancel each other out.

q: In SI units, force that is acting on 1 kg mass to give it an acceleration of $1 \text{ m s}^{-2}$ is called ____.
e: The newton (N) is the standard SI unit of force.

q: Similarly, in CGS system a force that is acting on 1 g mass to give it an acceleration of $1 \text{ cm s}^{-2}$ is called ____.
e: The dyne is the unit of force in the centimeter-gram-second (CGS) system.

q: In FPS system the unit of force is ____.
e: The pound (lb) is the unit of force in the foot-pound-second (FPS) system.

q: The ____ is the unit of mass in British engineering system.
e: The slug is defined as the mass that accelerates at $1 \text{ ft s}^{-2}$ when a force of 1 pound is applied.

q: Everybody attracts ____ in the universe.
e: Gravitational force is a universal attractive force between all masses.

q: The gravitational force between the two bodies is directly proportional to the product of the masses and ____ between them.
c: inversely proportional to the square of the distance
e: This inverse square relationship is a fundamental characteristic of Newton's law of gravitation.

q: In symbols, ____
e: This proportionality shows that gravitational force increases with mass and decreases with the square of the distance.

q: According to experimental measurements the value of G in MKS system is found to be ____.
e: G is the universal gravitational constant, which has the same value everywhere in the universe.

q: where G is a ____ which is the same for all bodies in the universe.
e: The universal gravitational constant does not change regardless of the masses or distance involved.

q: The attractions of the moon and the sun upon water of the earth cause ____.
e: Tides are a direct observable effect of the gravitational pull of celestial bodies on Earth's oceans.

q: Satellites are kept in their circular orbit by the ____ of the earth.
e: Earth's gravity provides the necessary centripetal force to keep satellites in orbit.

q: Four fundamental forces in nature are all ____.
e: Fundamental forces act over a distance through fields, without requiring physical contact.

q: They are the gravitational force, weak force, ____ and nuclear force.
e: The electromagnetic force is one of the four fundamental forces of nature.

q: ____ is the strongest and the gravitational force is the weakest of these forces.
e: The strong nuclear force binds protons and neutrons together in the atomic nucleus.

q: Among the four forces the gravitational and the electromagnetic forces are ____ and the remaining two forces are short-range forces.
e: Long-range forces have an infinite effective range, though their strength decreases with distance.

q: The electromagnetic force acts between ____.
e: Electromagnetic forces govern the interactions between charged particles.

q: Weak force acts between ____.
e: The weak force is responsible for processes like beta decay in subatomic particles.

q: Strong nuclear force acts between ____ such as proton, neutron, pion and strange particles.
e: The strong nuclear force binds elementary particles together to form hadrons.

q: However, unlike gravitational force, these two mechanical forces are not ____.
e: Frictional and elastic forces are macroscopic manifestations of electromagnetic forces at the atomic level.

q: When a spring is stretched (or) a plastic ruler is bent, the force that causes the spring and the ruler to retain their original form is called ____.
e: Elastic force is a restoring force that attempts to return a deformed object to its original shape.

q: The force that acts to resist the motion of the body is ____.
e: Frictional force opposes the relative motion between two surfaces in contact.

q: The weight of body is the ____ acting on it which gives its acceleration when it is falling.
e: Weight is specifically the gravitational force exerted by the Earth on a body.

q: The acceleration due to the earth's attraction is called ____ and it is represented by the symbol g.
e: Acceleration due to gravity is the rate at which an object accelerates when falling freely near the Earth's surface.

q: In FPS system, ____.
e: In the foot-pound-second system, the acceleration due to gravity is approximately 32 feet per second squared.

q: The attracting force of the earth acting on a body is defined as the ____ of the body.
e: Weight is a force, distinct from mass, and depends on the local gravitational field.

q: The gravitational force acting on the body (or) the weight of the body is found to be ____.
e: This equation calculates weight by multiplying the object's mass by the acceleration due to gravity.

q: Weight is a ____ and is directed toward the center of the Earth.
e: As a force, weight has both magnitude and direction, making it a vector quantity.

q: Mass is the ____ in a body.
e: Mass represents the amount of material an object contains and is a scalar quantity.

q: Mass is also a ____.
e: The greater the mass of an object, the greater its resistance to changes in motion.

q: The mass of a body defined from this point of view is called ____ while the mass defined by $m = \frac{W}{g}$ is called gravitational mass.
e: Inertial mass is determined by an object's resistance to acceleration when a force is applied.

q: Wherever a body may be, there is no change in the value of the ____ of the body.
e: Mass is an intrinsic property of an object and does not change with location.

q: But the ____ of the body can change.
e: Weight changes depending on the local acceleration due to gravity, such as on different planets.

q: Mass is a ____ and always a constant.
e: Unlike weight, mass has magnitude only and does not change with location.

q: If a body is dropped from a height near the earth's surface, the body will fall with a ____.
e: Near the Earth's surface, freely falling objects experience a nearly constant downward acceleration.

q: If the ____ is neglected, the fall of the body is defined as free fall.
e: Free fall assumes that gravity is the only force acting on the object.

q: Equation of motion under ____ described in chapter 2 can be used in the free fall.
e: The standard kinematic equations apply to free fall because the acceleration due to gravity is constant.

q: In these equations we will use the symbol ____ for displacement s and g for acceleration a.
e: In free fall problems, vertical displacement is typically represented by the variable h (height).

q: Hence, the equations become $v = v_0 + gt$ and ____
e: This is the third kinematic equation adapted for free fall, relating velocity, initial velocity, acceleration, and displacement.

q: Note that the acceleration due to gravity g is directed ____ (towards the centre of the earth).
e: Gravity always pulls objects toward the center of the Earth.

q: Since acceleration g is always directed downwards its value will be ____ (i.e. $g = -9.8 \text{ ms}^{-2}$).
e: In a coordinate system where upward is positive, the downward acceleration of gravity is assigned a negative value.

q: Momentum (p) of a body is defined as the ____, which is written as $p=mv$.
c: product of the mass of the body and its velocity
e: Momentum quantifies the amount of motion an object has, depending on both its mass and speed.

q: Momentum of a body is ____ to its velocity.
e: For a given mass, an increase in velocity results in a proportional increase in momentum.

q: Momentum is a ____.
e: Because velocity is a vector, momentum also has both magnitude and direction.

q: Direction of momentum is the same as that of ____.
e: Since mass is a positive scalar, the momentum vector points in the exact same direction as the velocity vector.

q: Unit of momentum is expressed as the ____.
c: product of mass unit and velocity unit
e: The unit of momentum is derived directly from its definition as mass times velocity.

q: In MKS system it is ____.
e: Kilogram meter per second is the standard SI unit for momentum.

q: One fundamental law of physics is the ____.
e: This law states that the total momentum of an isolated system remains constant if no external forces act on it.

q: This law states that: If there is no net external force acting on an ____, the total momentum of the system is constant.
e: An isolated system is one that does not interact with its surroundings, meaning no external forces are applied.

q: The law of conservation of momentum is a general law and is true for both ____ objects.
e: Conservation of momentum applies universally, from colliding billiard balls to subatomic particle interactions.

q: According to law of conservation of momentum, ____ = total momentum after collision.
e: In any collision within an isolated system, the sum of momenta before the event equals the sum of momenta after.
